text:
rita: saw an uptick in host CPU after last night's runtime rollout, p99 write latency jumped. perf-bot: alert: host-proxy write-latency p99 > 50ms (1m) - check 3265432100
owen: quick glance at traces shows lots of tiny frames from tokenizer -> streaming; writev syscalls are dominating.
neel: pprof snippet (20s sample):
 40  40%  sys_writev
 15  15%  ingress::frame_serialize
 10  10%  grpc::writer::flush_small
 8    8%  tokenizer::emit
5    5%  kv_cache::lookup_miss
rita: request histogram by size: <256B requests are 30% of traffic and have lower kv hit-rate.
owen: hypothesis: token emitter creates per-token frames for short completions; proxy isn't coalescing, so kernel sees many small writev calls -> syscalls overhead. also per-frame metadata lookups cause extra KV pressure.
neel: repro: quick script sending 1500 tiny streaming requests reproduces the spike.
rita: quick mitigations: (1) add a 1ms/3kB coalescing window in proxy write path, (2) add an ultra-light per-connection LRU (64 entries) for KV metadata to reduce misses on micro-requests. both low-risk.
owen: I'll land minimal coalesce PR (buffer flush at 1ms or 3kB) and run A/B.
neel: I'll add tracing tags: kv_hit=true/false per request and syscall_count sample.
perf-bot: reminder scheduled at 3265435700
rita: notes for longer term: runtime batching heuristics should avoid emitting frames for single-token responses where possible and prefer inline single-message responses. also consider tuning gRPC flow-control settings to reduce small-frame overhead.
owen: also testing tcp_nodelay toggle; turning it off reduced syscall rate but increased p50 slightly. will share numbers.
neel: for the mini-cache, keep it bounded and per-connection to avoid cross-tenant leakage; simple LRU of 32-64 entries should be fine.
rita: action items: owen -> coalesce PR (ETA 6h), neel -> kv/tracing tags (ETA 4h), rita -> canary config and rollout (ETA 2h). will reconvene in #eng-runtime after canary. :white_check_mark:
